plastic_crate_01.description: Free 4K model of a deep red plastic crate with lattice sides, cutout handles, and a worn GALLER STORAGE print. Realistic scuffs, grime, and sturdy ribs.

plastic_crate_02.description: Free 4K model of a rugged plastic crate with vented sides, stackable ribs, and cutout handles. Adjustable color with subtle scuffs and molded seams.

plastic_crate_03.description: Free 8K model of a weathered red plastic crate with lattice sides, ribbed frame, open handles, and realistic scuffs, grime, and edge wear.

wooden_crate_01.description: Free 8K model of a vintage wooden crate - weathered colonial chest with rope handles, metal rivets and latch; ideal as maritime, farmhouse or prop container.

wooden_crate_02.description: Free 8K model of a vintage wooden crate with worn planks, dovetail joins, brass corner plates and rope handles - ideal for maritime, colonial or farmhouse props.

night.note: the crates stand in the grocer's doorway recess, outside the lamp pools; the red plastic reads near black under the lantern colour (1, 0.25, 0) with a glint on the rim's top edge and on the bottles' glass

text.dairy_note: invented; named for the town's Copper Row district; moulded on the front band of each crate in raised capitals 18 mm tall, 2 mm proud, and embossed on each bottle's shoulder in 6 mm capitals; no logo, no real dairy's name, no cow, no price
text.band_text: COPPER ROW DAIRY | PROPERTY OF THE DAIRY | THIS CRATE IS NOT TO BE USED FOR ANY OTHER PURPOSE

placement.slot: east side, bay 5 (the grocer, x 33 to 39): one stack of three crates against the shopfront at the grocer's side-door end, x 38.0, back 0.05 m clear of the stallriser line (z 4.975), long side facing the road; a second, single crate (MC1) is the street's spare, not placed
placement.milk_float: yes: Quay Street's grocer and the tea room are doorstep customers of the dairy (a 1990 fact of British shops; Judgement, no source in canon names a float): the empties are put out for collection at the shop door; no milk float is drawn (the cars ruling), only its crates
reasons: crates stand at the shop that sells milk: the grocer (bay 5) takes a daily delivery; the stack stands 50 mm clear of the stallriser line (z 4.975) so it never leans on the glass, its 298 mm width taking 4.627 to 4.925 of the footway and leaving 1.50 m clear from the kerb's back edge (3.125)
it stands at the shop's side-door end (x 38.0) beside the litter and bin traffic of the east parade's end, 4 m from the chandler's door at x 40
the scene's yard-mouth crates are wooden and stay (one family's yard stuff); these are the grocer's

wear: the plastic is scuffed white along the rim's top edge and the lugs, and along the base rail's lower edge where crates are dragged; the faded top rim is chalkier than the body
dirt in every slot and in the floor's drain slots (a darker mask), a milky film on the floor under the bottles, a dried ring where bottles stood
the bottles: cap-less, a dull ring on each lip, embossed shoulder, a smear of old milk inside the lowest 10 mm (a mask on the glass)

one crate in the stack is a different colour (blue) from the other two: crates were swapped between dairies' rounds only within a dairy, so the stack is one colour in the sample and a blue one is a variant
NOT shown: any lettering but the dairy's name, a person, any other drink, a sticker

disagreements.photo: S2 shows 2021 plastic bottles; 1990's were glass pints
disagreements.chose: glass pint bottles, empty, no cap, an embossed fictional name

disagreements.photo: S2 shows the upper crate's base resting on the lower crate's rim with the lugs inside
disagreements.chose: pitch = crate height 264, lugs 9 high entering the next floor

variants_note: MC3 (the sample): three crates, six empty pint bottles in the top one, one colour (red).
MC1: a single crate, empty (a spare for the yard or a doorstep).
colours: red (the sample), blue, yellow, green, orange (a dairy's crates are all one colour); fade and grime as wear.
a crate on its side or two stacked with bottles in the lower one (a seed, not a mesh): the builder may place the MC1 mesh as it likes.
not_settled: no photograph of a 1975 to 1995 crate was reached; P1 is a 2021 oblique view, so the slot layout, the rim depth (28 mm, error 12) and the name band (66 mm, error 12) are judged; the box is Poly Haven's measured 298 x 408 x 264

whether a 1990 12-pint crate is 264 high (the CC0 record, a storage crate tagged milk crate) or nearer 200: the bottles then stand fully inside (their tops 70 mm below the rim); one number for the builder to confirm against a period crate if one is ever reached
the crate's slot sizes and the floor's drain slots (36 slots 20 x 8 are a Judgement written as a texture mask, not geometry)
whether a milk float served Quay Street: stated as a Judgement; the empties are the only sign of it
the pint bottle's exact shape (body 64 across, neck 28, 184 high: Judgement)
content_rule_note: milk, not drink: no beer, wine or spirit bottle, no crate with a drinks brand, no person (a statement of the content rule).
builder_notes: build the crate by script in one mesh: floor plate with 36 drain slots cut (a mask or real holes), four walls as ribs and slots (the gaps between the ribs are open), rim, base rail with four recesses under the corners for the lugs, name band with the raised text
stack by instancing the crate at z 0, 264, 528 (no scale), rotate each crate by a seed of 0 to 2 degrees about z (not more: they interlock)
bottles: glass, a body 128 and neck 56 with a lip ring; six in the top crate in a 4 x 3 grid of 100 mm cells (six of the twelve cells)
texture: our own colour map for the crate; the CC0 model's texture is NOT used (its lettering)
